name: Beef, white bean, and chard soup
time: About 2½ hours, almost all of it simmering
intro: November's first soup, and the week's make-ahead: beef chuck browned hard and simmered until it falls apart, with leeks, white beans, and a whole bunch of chard. Made on Sunday, it's dinner twice and lunch through the week, with a few bowls for the freezer.
needs: 2½ lbs boneless beef chuck roast, in 1½-inch pieces
1 bunch Swiss chard, stems chopped, leaves torn
1 carton (4 cups) chicken stock, plus 4 cups water
A Parmesan rind, if your wedge has one, and grated Parmesan to serve
Salt, black pepper, and chile flakes

steps.text: Pat the beef dry and salt it well.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown the beef in two or three batches, without crowding, until it's dark on at least two sides. Move each batch to a bowl.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the leeks, chard stems, and a pinch of salt and cook until soft. Add the garlic and a pinch of chile flakes for the last minute.
Pour in the stock and water and scrape the bottom clean. Return the beef and its juices, add the Parmesan rind, and bring to a simmer.
Cover with the lid slightly ajar and keep it at a gentle simmer — a few lazy bubbles, never a boil — until the beef breaks apart when pressed with a spoon.
Add the beans and simmer uncovered so the broth thickens a little.
Stir in the chard leaves until they wilt. Take out the rind, squeeze in half the lemon, and season with salt and pepper.
Grated Parmesan, black pepper, and a forkful of pickled fennel on top. Cool the rest quickly, refrigerate it within 2 hours, and freeze what you won't eat in four days.

how_it_works: Chuck is a hard-working shoulder muscle full of connective tissue; a hot pan makes it tough, but two hours at a gentle simmer melts that tissue into the broth, which is why the meat goes soft and the soup tastes rich. Browning first is what makes it taste like beef rather than boiled meat. Beans and chard go in late, so they hold their shape.
swaps: Bone-in chicken thighs instead of beef; they're tender in about 45 minutes.
Cauliflower florets with the beans for a thicker soup.
A spoonful of melted leeks on top instead of the lemon.
leftovers: It keeps four days in the fridge and three months in the freezer, and it's better on day two. Reheat a bowl until it's steaming, and add a little water if it has thickened.
